title: USC4AM event and Oakland County expense verification analysis
summary: Primary Center pages confirm relevant Milwaukee and Texas events, narrowing the issue from possible fictitious conference travel to incomplete public reimbursement support and unresolved attendance records.

data.question: Do primary USC4AM records corroborate the Oakland County conference-trip descriptions, and what accountability questions remain?
data.method: Cross-source event, date, location, governance and current-role reconciliation using official Center and county pages plus attributed expense reporting.
data.framework: Separate event existence, attendance, reimbursable business purpose, documentation completeness, policy compliance and misconduct allegations.
data.scope: USC4AM Milwaukee and Texas 2023 events, Oakland County governance and public reporting reviewed through 2026-07-27.
findings: USC4AM officially confirms a May 15–16, 2023 Milwaukee strategy event at GE HealthCare Institute and Marquette University.
USC4AM officially confirms a final 2023 digital-transformation strategy event in Texas hosted with Flex; its Milwaukee recap scheduled that event for November 13–14.
These event records materially corroborate the reported conference purposes but do not publish complete attendee lists or county travel records.
The accountability issue is therefore incomplete reimbursement support and unresolved attendance/compliance, not absence of a real event.
David Woodward remains Oakland County Board Chair and is currently listed as a USC4AM executive-committee public-sector member alongside WEF Managing Director Kiva Allgood.
Sean Carlson left Oakland County on April 7, 2026 despite a county contact page that still lists him.
conclusions: The Milwaukee trip purpose is strongly corroborated by a primary event record.
The Austin trip is probably connected to the official Texas Flex event, but city-level venue and attendance remain unconfirmed.
No public evidence reviewed establishes fraud, corruption, fictitious travel or improper personal benefit from these two conference trips.
Primary county records remain necessary to determine policy compliance, approval authority, receipt completeness and charged-item validity.
recommendations: Obtain the underlying Oakland County travel authorizations, expense reports, receipts and approver signatures.
Request USC4AM attendee rosters, agendas and executive-committee minutes for the Milwaukee and Texas events.
Reconcile charged travel dates and locations against official event schedules.
Correct stale Oakland County personnel pages and track Carlson as a former official after April 7, 2026.
counterarguments: A real event does not prove every charged expense was necessary or compliant.
Missing conference attachments in a reimbursement packet may reflect clerical incompleteness rather than misconduct.
Secondary reporting may omit documents that exist elsewhere in county systems.
limitations: No primary expense packet or FOIA production was obtained directly.
The official Texas page does not name Austin.
No complete official attendee list was found.
Current WXYZ reporting concerns broader travel patterns and cannot be attributed wholesale to USC4AM.
unresolved: Exact Texas venue and charged travel dates.
Carlson and Woodward attendance records for both events.
Funding source for each trip and each charged item.

caveats: Trip-event matching is not equivalent to reimbursement validation.

workflow.next_action: Obtain and reconcile primary county expense, attendance and governance records.
